title: AgentSWE: Can Coding Agents Build the Agent You Actually Want?
title_zh: AgentSWE：编码智能体能否构建出你真正想要的智能体？

paragraphs.en: As the production of software passes into the hands of software itself, coding agents are increasingly commissioned to build agents fitted to their users’ own workflows. This delegation carries a quiet assumption, that the delivered agent will faithfully serve the requirement it was built for, rather than merely appear to. No existing benchmark tests that assumption. We introduce AgentSWE , a benchmark for agent software engineering spanning three stages of the agent development lifecycle: Creation of a complete agent from a natural-language requirement, Editing of production agent codebases, and Optimization toward a measurable target. Each of its 25 tasks is framed as a commission rather than an exam: the builder iterates against a handful of illustrative cases, while acceptance exercises the frozen submission on held-out cases designed to span the full requirement, grading behavior against requirement-derived rubrics under hard pass/fail gates or, for Optimization, against the source benchmark’s own objective. Evaluating a range of coding agents across models and harnesses, we find that none comes close to delivering what a requirement asks for: the gap between what a builder demonstrates and what it delivers is the norm, not the corner case. An accompanying empirical analysis of the failure trajectories identifies recurring failure modes, among them overfitting to the visible cases, hollow runtimes behind code that looks complete, and unsupported claims of completion, each a signal by which coding agents can learn to build the agents they are asked for.

paragraphs.en: Coding agents such as Claude Code ( Anthropic, 2026 ) and Codex ( OpenAI, 2026a ) now carry substantial engineering workloads ( Chen et al., 2021 ; Yang et al., 2024b ; Wang et al., 2025b ) , and many of their users are not engineers: they describe what they need and delegate the rest ( Hitzig et al., 2026 ) . Increasingly, what they delegate is the building of an agent, a program that wraps a model, tools, and state around one recurring job so that the job runs on a fixed runtime, at a fixed cost, without a coding agent attending each run. Delegation of this kind rests on trust: that a coding agent, handed a requirement in natural language, will deliver the agent its user intends rather than one that merely appears to comply. Whether that trust is warranted is what this paper measures.

paragraphs.en: Agent development spans three stages. It begins with creation , where a natural-language requirement must become a working system; continues through editing , where new capabilities join a living codebase without unsettling what already works; and matures into optimization , where the agent is pushed toward an explicit target, be it a public leaderboard or a production workload. Handing this lifecycle to coding agents invites failures subtler than broken code: an agent that passes visible examples yet misses the intent behind them ( Liu et al., 2023 ; Zhao et al., 2026a ; Lodkaew et al., 2026 ) ; a tool registered but never invoked ( Soni, 2026 ; Fan et al., 2026 ) ; a goal that drifts over a long horizon ( Arike et al., 2025 ; Menon et al., 2026 ) ; a report citing evidence no source contains ( Onweller et al., 2026 ; Rao et al., 2026 ) . Such failures are not hypothetical; they are the present condition of agent-built agents ( Raj et al., 2026 ; Naik et al., 2026 ) . The questions are how far coding agents compromise the requirements they are handed, on which capabilities, and for what reasons.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体开发涵盖三个阶段。 第一阶段是创建，此时自然语言需求必须转化为一个可运行的系统；第二阶段是编辑，新能力被整合到动态演变的代码库中，同时不会干扰已正常运行的部分；第三阶段则是优化，智能体在此阶段朝着明确的目标推进，无论是公开排行榜还是实际生产任务。 将这一生命周期交由编码智能体处理，可能会引发比代码错误更隐蔽的问题：智能体可能通过可见的测试用例，却未能理解其背后的意图（Liu et al., 2023；Zhao et al., 2026a；Lodkaew et al., 2026）；工具可能被注册却从未被调用（Soni, 2026；Fan et al., 2026）；目标在长期执行过程中发生偏移（Arike et al., 2025；Menon et al., 2026）；报告引用了来源中并不存在的证据（Onweller et al., 2026；Rao et al., 2026）。 这类失败并非假设，而是智能体所构建的智能体的现实状况（Raj et al., 2026；Naik et al., 2026）。 关键问题在于：编码智能体会在多大程度上偏离其被赋予的需求？哪些能力会受到影响？原因又是什么？

paragraphs.en: These questions outrun the instruments we have. SWE-bench and its descendants grade the repair of conventional software against a reference patch or test suite ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ; Chan et al., 2024 ) ; NL2Repo-Bench commissions whole repositories from requirement documents ( Ding et al., 2025 ) ; Paper2Code and PaperBench rebuild research implementations checked against the papers they reproduce ( Seo et al., 2025 ; Starace et al., 2025 ) . Each judges ordinary code against an answer known in advance. A commissioned agent wraps a stochastic policy around tools, answers to a requirement that has no reference solution, and keeps changing after delivery. Benchmarks that do evaluate agents, from AgentBench onward ( Liu et al., 2024 ) , examine a finished agent and ask how well it performs; none asks whether a coding agent could have built it. Work on agents that design or improve other agents ( Hu et al., 2025 ; Mishra et al., 2026 ) comes closest, but it measures how far a search procedure or a meta-agent can raise a benchmark score, not whether a general coding agent delivers the agent a requirement describes ( Section 2 ). Between judging built software and judging finished agents lies a step that current suites leave unmeasured: building the agent that a requirement asks for.
paragraphs.zh: 这些问题超出了我们现有工具的能力范围。 SWE-bench 及其后续版本通过参考补丁或测试套件来评估传统软件的修复效果（Jimenez 等人，2024；Chan 等人，2024）；NL2Repo-Bench 根据需求文档生成完整的代码库（Ding 等人，2025）；Paper2Code 和 PaperBench 则重建研究论文中的实现，并与原始论文进行比对验证（Seo 等人，2025；Starace 等人，2025）。 每种方法都基于一个预先已知正确答案的标准来评估常规代码。 一个受委托的智能体将随机策略与工具结合，用以回应一个没有参考解决方案的需求，并且在交付后仍会持续调整。 从 AgentBench 开始（Liu 等人，2024），那些评估智能体的基准测试都会检查一个已完成的智能体及其表现，但没有一个会追问：编码智能体是否本应能够构建出它。 研究设计或改进其他智能体的工作（Hu 等人，2025；Mishra 等人，2026）与此最为接近，但这些研究衡量的是搜索过程或元智能体能在多大程度上提升基准得分，而非一个通用编码智能体是否真正实现了需求所描述的智能体（第 2 节）。 在评估已构建的软件与评估已完成智能体之间，存在一个当前测试套件尚未测量的关键步骤：即构建需求所要求的那个智能体本身。

paragraphs.en: We introduce AgentSWE , a benchmark that turns faithful delegation from anecdote into measurement ( Figure 1 ) through three commitments. The first is to measure the whole lifecycle, through twenty-five tasks spanning all three stages. Ten Creation tasks commission a complete agent from a natural-language requirement, over workloads from GUI automation to formal theorem proving, each scoped against a mature open-source system; ten Editing tasks ask for new capabilities in the pinned codebase of a production agent such as OpenHands or Aider, capabilities that cut through crash recovery, permission fencing, and transactional state; and five Optimization tasks set a working agent against a measurable target. The second commitment is that evaluation should mirror the delegation it studies. Each task is framed as a commission: the builder sees only what a customer could provide, while acceptance also tests the stated clauses its examples leave out. The builder develops against the requirement and a few illustrative cases; held-out cases then test the frozen delivery in isolation. The third commitment follows from the absence of a prescribed reference implementation: every Creation and Editing execution is graded against a rubric derived from the requirement itself, and hard gates assign zero to invalid executions and inapplicable patches.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 AgentSWE——一个基准测试，它通过三项承诺，将忠实的委托从轶事转化为可测量的指标（图 1）。 第一项承诺是测量整个生命周期，涵盖跨越全部三个阶段的二十五个任务。 十个“创建”任务要求智能体根据自然语言需求完成完整开发，任务范围涵盖 GUI 自动化到形式化定理证明，每个任务都以成熟的开源系统为限定；十个“编辑”任务则要求在 OpenHands 或 Aider 等生产级智能体的固定代码库中实现新功能，这些功能需具备崩溃恢复、权限隔离和事务状态管理能力；五个“优化”任务则将运行中的智能体与可量化的目标进行对比。 第二项承诺是评估过程必须与其所研究的委托机制保持一致。 每个任务都被设计为一种委托：构建者仅能看到客户可能提供的信息，而验收环节还会测试其示例中未涵盖的明确条款。 构建者根据需求及若干示例案例进行开发；随后，预留的案例将独立测试最终交付成果。 第三项承诺源于没有预设参考实现这一前提：所有“创建”和“编辑”任务的执行结果都将依据从需求本身推导出的评分标准进行评判，而严格判罚机制会对无效执行和不适用的补丁给予零分。

sents.en: Each task is framed as a commission: the builder sees only what a customer could provide, while acceptance also tests the stated clauses its examples leave out.
sents.zh: 每个任务都被设计为一种委托：构建者仅能看到客户可能提供的信息，而验收环节还会测试其示例中未涵盖的明确条款。

sents.en: The builder develops against the requirement and a few illustrative cases; held-out cases then test the frozen delivery in isolation.
sents.zh: 构建者根据需求及若干示例案例进行开发；随后，预留的案例将独立测试最终交付成果。

sents.en: The third commitment follows from the absence of a prescribed reference implementation: every Creation and Editing execution is graded against a rubric derived from the requirement itself, and hard gates assign zero to invalid executions and inapplicable patches.
sents.zh: 第三项承诺源于没有预设参考实现这一前提：所有“创建”和“编辑”任务的执行结果都将依据从需求本身推导出的评分标准进行评判，而严格判罚机制会对无效执行和不适用的补丁给予零分。

paragraphs.en: We put this instrument to work on five models as builders in the Codex harness, together with further pairings of harness and model. The verdict is sobering. The strongest builders average 19.1 on Creation and 31.6 on Editing, and in Optimization no builder closes more than 5 % of the remaining gap to the target on average, and only 13 of the 25 runs score above their starter. Creation runs that end development at 90 or above deliver agents averaging 9.9 on held-out cases. The gap between what a builder demonstrates and what it delivers is not the corner case of agent software engineering; it is the norm. The builders’ trajectories reveal recurring failures. Builders overfit to the visible development cases, and the delivery fails on the clauses those cases leave out; they ship hollow runtimes, code that reads as complete but does no work when run; and both builders and the agents they deliver claim completions that their own records contradict. Each of these modes names a habit that the next generation of coding agents can be built and trained to avoid. More development cases, a prescribed design, an instruction to test, and a longer case budget shift the scores but leave held-out Result low under every condition.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将该工具部署在五个模型上，使其作为 Codex 框架中的构建者运行，并尝试了其他框架与模型的组合。结果令人警醒。 最强的构建者在“创作”任务上的平均得分为 19.1，在“编辑”任务上为 31.6；而在“优化”任务中，没有任何构建者能平均缩小超过 5% 的剩余目标差距，且 25 次运行中仅有 13 次的得分高于初始水平。 在开发阶段达到 90 分或更高的“创作”运行所生成的智能体，在预留测试案例上的平均得分为 9.9。 构建者所展示的能力与其实际交付成果之间的差距，并非智能体软件工程中的极端个例，而是普遍现象。 构建者的发展轨迹揭示了反复出现的失败模式。 构建者会对可见的开发案例产生过拟合，导致交付成果在那些案例中未涵盖的条款上失效；它们产出的运行时空洞无物——代码看似完整，但运行后却无法执行任何操作；而且构建者及其生成的智能体都会声称完成了任务，尽管其自身记录却与此矛盾。 上述每种模式都揭示了一种习惯，下一代编码智能体可以被设计和训练以避免这种问题。 增加更多开发案例、采用规定的设计方案、加入测试指令以及延长案例预算，虽然会改变得分，但在所有条件下，预留测试的“结果”得分仍然偏低。

paragraphs.en: In sum, this paper makes three contributions. First, we formalize agent software engineering as a measurable problem, in which a builder must satisfy a requirement it can probe only through limited development feedback. Second, we deliver AgentSWE, twenty-five commissions whose acceptance executes the delivered agent on held-out cases and grades each run with a requirement-derived rubric or a native objective, and we evaluate various harness–model pairings against it. Third, we contribute an empirical analysis of the failure trajectories, which identifies recurring failure modes of coding agents and turns each into a direction for the next generation of coding agents.
paragraphs.zh: 总而言之，本文提出了三项贡献。 首先，我们将智能体软件工程形式化为一个可测量的问题：构建者必须满足一项只能通过有限开发反馈来探知的需求。 其次，我们推出了 AgentSWE——由二十五个任务组成，通过执行这些任务，系统会在预留测试用例上运行所交付的智能体，并使用源自需求的评分标准或原生目标对每次运行进行评级；我们还基于此评估了多种工具与模型的组合。 第三，我们提供了一项关于失败轨迹的经验性分析，该分析识别出编码智能体的常见失败模式，并将每种模式转化为下一代编码智能体的发展方向。

paragraphs.en: Research on automated agent development has expanded both the scope of what can be designed and the stage at which adaptation occurs. Early approaches generate task-specific roles, tools, and collaboration patterns from task descriptions or seed agents ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Yuan et al., 2025 ; Tang et al., 2026 ) . Subsequent work formulates agent development as optimization, first over textual components such as instructions and demonstrations ( Yang et al., 2024a ; Khattab et al., 2023 ; Agrawal et al., 2025 ) , and then over broader design spaces containing agent modules, communication structures, and executable workflows ( Zhuge et al., 2024 ; Shang et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025c ; Zhang et al., 2025a ; Zhou et al., 2025 ) . This paradigm has further expanded to searching over complete code-defined agents and multi-agent scaffolds ( Hu et al., 2025 ; Rosser & Foerster, 2025 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 关于自动化智能体开发的研究，既拓展了可设计内容的范围，也改变了适应发生的阶段。 早期的方法从任务描述或初始智能体中生成特定于任务的角色、工具和合作模式（Chen et al., 2024；Yuan et al., 2025；Tang et al., 2026）。 后续研究将智能体开发表述为优化问题：首先针对指令和演示等文本组件进行优化（Yang et al., 2024a；Khattab et al., 2023；Agrawal et al., 2025），随后扩展到包含智能体模块、通信结构和可执行工作流的更广泛设计空间（Zhuge et al., 2024；Shang et al., 2025；Zhang et al., 2025c；Zhang et al., 2025a；Zhou et al., 2025）。 这一范式进一步扩展到了对完整代码定义的智能体和多智能体框架的搜索（Hu et al., 2025；Rosser & Foerster, 2025）。

paragraphs.en: A related line relaxes the assumption that the improvement procedure itself remains fixed. Initial systems support self-referential modification of an improver or agent logic ( Zelikman et al., 2023 ; Yin et al., 2025 ) , while later approaches expose complete implementations, harnesses, and meta-level improvement mechanisms to revision ( Robeyns et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ; Wang et al., 2025a ; Zhang et al., 2026b ; Lee et al., 2026 ; Hebbar et al., 2026 ) . Arbor ( Jin et al., 2026 ) carries hypotheses and evidence across long-horizon artifact optimization, whereas JIT-Agent ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) synthesizes task-conditioned executable harnesses at inference time. Together, these developments establish agent construction and optimization as a capability in its own right. AgentSWE makes this capability the object of evaluation, measuring whether general-purpose coding agents can create, modify, and optimize agents from heterogeneous user requirements.
paragraphs.zh: 相关研究放宽了这样一个假设：改进过程本身保持固定不变。 早期系统支持对改进器或智能体逻辑进行自指性修改（Zelikman 等，2023；Yin 等，2025），而后续方法则让完整的实现、执行框架和元层改进机制能够接受修订（Robeyns 等，2025；Zhang 等，2025b；Wang 等，2025a；Zhang 等，2026b；Lee 等，2026；Hebbar 等，2026）。 Arbor（Jin 等，2026）在长期人工制品优化过程中贯穿假设与证据，而 JIT-Agent（Zhang 等，2026a）则在推理时合成任务相关的可执行执行框架。 这些进展共同确立了智能体构建与优化作为一项独立能力的地位。 AgentSWE 将这一能力本身作为评估对象，旨在衡量通用编码智能体是否能够根据用户提供的异构需求创建、修改和优化智能体。

paragraphs.en: Most agent benchmarks hold the agent implementation fixed and evaluate its performance within a given environment. Recent benchmarks move beyond task completion by asking agents to construct or iteratively improve more complex artifacts. WorFBench ( Qiao et al., 2025 ) evaluates generated workflow structures, while benchmarks for machine-learning experimentation and research engineering evaluate improvement of executable research artifacts ( Huang et al., 2024 ; Nathani et al., 2025 ; Wijk et al., 2025 ) . AI4AI-Bench ( Chi et al., 2026 ) extends this setting to the redesign of model-training algorithms. Other evaluations isolate specific improvement mechanisms: SE-Bench ( Yuan et al., 2026 ) studies knowledge internalization, whereas OPT-BENCH ( Li et al., 2026 ) measures feedback-driven solution refinement. These benchmarks evaluate workflows, research artifacts, or optimized solutions rather than deployable agents.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数智能体基准测试都会固定智能体的实现方式，并在特定环境中评估其性能。 近期的基准测试不再局限于任务完成，而是要求智能体构建或迭代改进更复杂的成果物。 WorFBench（Qiao 等，2025）评估生成的工作流结构，而针对机器学习实验和研究工程的基准测试则评估可执行研究成果物的改进程度（Huang 等，2024；Nathani 等，2025；Wijk 等，2025）。 AI4AI-Bench（Chi 等，2026）将这一设定扩展到了模型训练算法的重设计领域。 其他评估则聚焦于特定的改进机制：SE-Bench（Yuan 等，2026）研究知识内化过程，而 OPT-BENCH（Li 等，2026）则衡量基于反馈的解决方案优化程度。 这些基准测试评估的是工作流、研究成果物或优化后的解决方案，而非可直接部署的智能体。

paragraphs.en: Closest to our setting, AIE-Bench ( Mishra et al., 2026 ) evaluates whether a meta-agent can improve a pinned target-agent scaffold under controlled mutation boundaries and trial budgets. AgentSWE extends this setting to the full agent-development lifecycle: creating agents from natural-language commissions, modifying existing agent codebases without regression and optimizing working agents toward measurable objectives. By freezing submissions and evaluating their behavior on held-out cases, AgentSWE measures whether coding agents can deliver the agents users actually request.
paragraphs.zh: 与我们的设定最接近的是 AIE-Bench（Mishra 等人，2026），它评估元智能体是否能在受控的突变边界和试验预算下，改进一个固定的目标智能体框架。 AgentSWE 将这一设定扩展到了完整的智能体开发生命周期：根据自然语言指令创建智能体，在不引发回归的情况下修改现有智能体的代码库，并针对可量化的目标优化运行中的智能体。 通过冻结提交结果并在预留的测试案例上评估其行为，AgentSWE 衡量编码智能体能否交付用户实际所需的智能体。

paragraphs.en: A commission prescribes no reference implementation, so we define the requirement, the delivered agent, the builder, and the fidelity of a delivery through observable behavior alone.
paragraphs.zh: 委员会并未规定任何参考实现，因此我们仅通过可观察的行为来定义需求、交付的智能体、构建者以及交付的保真度。

paragraphs.en: A commission begins with a natural-language requirement q = ( g , ℐ , 𝒞 , ℛ ) q=(g,\mathcal{I},\mathcal{C},\mathcal{R}) , which every AgentSWE task publishes in four parts: the goal g g , which states what the agent is for and what counts as serving its user; the interface contract ℐ \mathcal{I} , which fixes how the agent is launched and which artifacts it must deliver; the constraints 𝒞 \mathcal{C} , which bound what may be edited, installed, or invoked; and the resources ℛ \mathcal{R} , such as data, repositories, and access to models and search. paragraphs.en: Harbor ( Harbor Framework Team, 2026 ) , a container framework for agent evaluation, runs the builder in one persistent session ( Figure 3 , left). The builder works in a private writable workspace and may submit a snapshot of its delivery at any time. Each snapshot runs on the development cases in isolated jobs, and the scores and summarized feedback return to the same session, within fixed time and submission budgets ( Appendix E ). Development ends when the builder exits or exhausts its submissions or its time budget. Creation then freezes the workspace; Editing freezes the last accepted submission, so a builder whose submissions were never accepted delivers nothing; Optimization freezes the accepted snapshot with the highest development objective. Freezing records the delivery and its software environment, and the held-out evaluation verifies that neither has changed.
paragraphs.zh: Harbor（Harbor Framework Team，2026）是一个用于智能体评估的容器框架，它在一个持久化会话中运行构建器（图3，左侧）。 构建器在私有的可写工作空间中运行，并且可以随时提交其交付内容的快照。 每个快照都在隔离的作业中运行开发用例，得分和总结性反馈会返回到同一会话，且受限于固定的时间和提交预算（附录E）。 当构建器退出或耗尽提交次数或时间预算时，开发阶段结束。 创建操作会冻结工作空间；编辑操作则会冻结最后被接受的提交，因此如果构建器的提交从未被接受，则不会交付任何内容；优化操作则会冻结具有最高开发目标的已接受快照。 冻结操作会记录交付内容及其软件环境，而预留的评估环节会验证这两者均未发生更改。

paragraphs.en: For Creation and Editing, deterministic gates first assign zero to an execution that does not launch, exceeds its time budget, or produces no parseable deliverable. A frontier reasoning model at its highest effort then applies the Result rubric ( Zheng et al., 2023 ; Arora et al., 2025 ) (GPT-5.6 Sol for Creation, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash ( DeepSeek-AI, 2026b ) for Editing; Table 9 ). The judge grades what the agent produced on one concrete case, its artifacts, execution trace, and resulting state, rather than the quality of its code, and ceilings bind the score to the violations the evaluator records. The task score is the mean partial-credit score over its held-out cases on a 0–100 scale, and family scores are macro-averages over tasks. Optimization instead scores the selected candidate and the starter with the native evaluator on the same held-out instances, a signal independent of the Result judge, and reports the gap closure of Equation 3 .

paragraphs.en: The builders that deliver on nearly every task, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GPT-5.5, and GPT-5.6 Sol, still realize only part of the commissioned capabilities: their means lie between 20 and 35, and only one run, GPT-5.5 on the Codex task, reaches 70. Qwen3.6 fails earlier: it submits no candidate on any task, typically ending its session right after announcing a plan. DeepSeek-V4-Flash delivers on four tasks; on most of the others it works until the budget runs out without ever submitting a candidate. Adding capabilities to a working product thus fails in two ways: the patch covers only part of the requirement, or the builder never finishes one.

paragraphs.en: Development scores overstate what a delivery does on the rest of the requirement, so the gap F D − F D ¯ F_{D}-F_{\bar{D}} of Section 3.2 is wide. paragraphs.en: Trajectories and artifacts reveal case-specific implementations: builders fit their agents to the visible cases in 14 of 25 Optimization runs and 13 of the 33 Editing runs that deliver. On PinchBench, DeepSeek-V4-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Pro route tasks by keyword to playbooks for visible task categories, gaining 8.1 and 59.4 points on development cases and losing 15.2 and 15.1 on held-out cases ( Appendix I ). Even explicit feedback leaves such defects unresolved: in eight of ten DeepSeek-V4-Pro Editing runs, development feedback names a violated requirement that the delivery still violates on held-out cases ( Section H.3 ). The requirement states what the held-out cases test; what fails is translating a requirement with interacting capabilities into an agent that generalizes beyond the visible cases.
paragraphs.zh: 轨迹和产物揭示了针对具体案例的实现方式：在 25 次优化运行中，构建者将智能体适配到 14 个可见案例；在 33 次编辑运行中，则适配到 13 个成功交付的可见案例。 在 PinchBench 上，DeepSeek-V4-Flash 和 DeepSeek-V4-Pro 通过关键词将任务路由至对应可见任务类别的操作指南，在开发案例上分别获得 8.1 分和 59.4 分，但在预留测试案例上分别损失了 15.2 分和 15.1 分（附录 I）。 即使有明确的反馈，这类缺陷仍未得到解决：在十次 DeepSeek-V4-Pro 编辑运行中，有八次的开发反馈指出了被违反的需求，而这些需求在预留测试案例中依然未被满足（H.3 节）。 该需求定义了预留测试案例所检验的内容；而失败之处在于，如何将一个涉及相互作用的复杂能力需求转化为能够超越可见案例进行泛化的智能体。

paragraphs.en: Code that reads as complete often does not work when run. paragraphs.en: Development cases are what builders overfit to ( Section 5.3 ). On two Creation tasks, with three builder runs per condition, we give the builder zero, one, two, or four of them. Going from zero to two development cases raises mean Result by 34.3 points on PDF translation and by 29.3 on PPTX generation ( Table 4 ); without any case, all three PDF deliveries score zero. Two further cases add nothing on PDF and lower PPTX from 33.5 to 15.2 ( Figure 7 ).
paragraphs.zh: 开发用例是构建者过度拟合的对象（第 5.3 节）。 在两个创建任务中，每个条件进行三次构建运行，我们向构建者提供零个、一个、两个或四个这样的用例。 将开发用例从零增加到两个，可使 PDF 翻译的平均结果提升 34.3 分，PPTX 生成结果提升 29.3 分（表 4）；若不提供任何用例，所有三个 PDF 交付物的得分均为零。 再增加两个用例对 PDF 没有提升作用，并使 PPTX 得分从 33.5 降至 15.2（图 7）。

paragraphs.en: We introduced AgentSWE to measure whether coding agents deliver agents that serve their requirement on cases they have not seen. Current builders rarely do: in the main comparison, the strongest average 19.1 on Creation and 31.6 on Editing, and in Optimization none closes more than 5 % of the remaining gap to the target on average. The trajectories reveal recurring failures: builders fit the visible cases, ship runtimes that read as complete but do not work, and, like the agents they deliver, claim completions their own records contradict. These failure modes chart where coding agents need to improve; our future work will pursue harnesses that test against the requirement and verify completion claims, and training that rewards behavior on unseen cases.
paragraphs.zh: 我们引入了 AgentSWE，用以衡量编码智能体所交付的智能体是否能够满足其未曾见过的用例需求。 当前的构建者很少做到这一点：在主对比中，最强的模型在“创建”任务上的平均得分为 19.1，在“编辑”任务上为 31.6；而在“优化”任务中，没有任何模型的平均得分能缩小与目标之间超过 5% 的差距。 这些发展轨迹揭示了反复出现的失败模式：构建者会针对可见的用例进行适配，交付看似完整实则无法运行的程序，并且像它们所交付的智能体一样，声称完成了某些其自身记录却相矛盾的任务。 这些失败模式指明了编码智能体需要改进的方向；我们未来的工作将致力于开发能够依据需求进行测试并验证完成声明的工具，以及针对未见用例的行为进行奖励的训练方法。

paragraphs.en: We used generative AI tools for three tasks. First, to construct the benchmark, we used Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol to synthesize task materials from the analyzed source systems ( Section 4.1 ): the requirement documents, the development and held-out cases, and the task-specific Result rubrics. The authors designed each commission and reviewed and revised the generated materials. Second, AI agents assisted the trajectory analysis ( Sections 5.3 and H ) by labeling failure modes from builder trajectories, execution traces, and evaluator records; the authors reviewed the labels and the resulting counts. Third, we used AI assistants to aid and polish the writing of this paper. Coding agents and language models are also the object of study, acting as builders, runtime models, and judges ( Sections 5.1 and E ); this use is part of the method rather than assistance to the authors. We have reviewed all AI-assisted content and take full responsibility for the paper.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用生成式人工智能工具完成了三项任务。 首先，为了构建基准测试，我们使用 Codex 和 GPT-5.6 Sol 从已分析的来源系统（第 4.1 节）中合成任务材料：需求文档、开发及预留用例，以及任务特定的结果评分标准。 作者们设计了每一项委托，并对生成的材料进行了审核与修订。 其次，人工智能智能体通过标注构建者轨迹、执行痕迹和评估者记录中的失败模式，辅助了轨迹分析（第 5.3 节和第 H 节）；作者们审核了这些标签及由此得出的统计结果。 第三，我们使用人工智能助手来协助并润色本文的写作。 编码智能体和语言模型也是研究对象，它们分别扮演构建者、运行时模型和评判者的角色（第 5.1 节和第 E 节）；这种使用方式属于方法本身的一部分，而非对作者的辅助。 我们已经审核了所有由人工智能协助生成的内容，并对本文承担全部责任。

paragraphs.en: AgentSWE asks coding agents to build agents that execute code, access the web, and, in one Creation task, validate software vulnerabilities. All builder sessions and candidate executions run in isolated containers with pinned fixtures, and every model call passes through a benchmark-owned gateway ( Appendix D ). The benchmark involves no human subjects. Its tasks derive from public repositories and public benchmarks, used under their licenses and terms. Our analysis documents how coding agents misreport their own work, which we regard as a safety-relevant property of delegating software to them.
paragraphs.zh: AgentSWE 要求编码智能体构建能够执行代码、访问网络，并在某项创建任务中验证软件漏洞的智能体。 所有构建会话和候选执行均在隔离容器中运行，并固定了环境配置；每次模型调用均需经过由基准测试管理的网关（附录 D）。 该基准测试不涉及任何人类受试者。 其任务源自公开仓库和公开基准测试，并在遵循相应许可协议与条款的前提下使用。 我们的分析记录了编码智能体如何错误报告自身的工作成果，我们认为这是将软件委托给它们时一项与安全相关的特性。

paragraphs.en: The six Result dimensions allocate 35 points to semantic completeness and terminology, 35 to fidelity of scientific objects and data, 12 to page and reading structure, 8 to alignment auditability, 8 to the offline viewer, and 2 to delivery integrity and accessibility, so 70 points concern the translated content. The evaluator checks the final bundle, the rendered pages and their geometry, and the viewer in a browser; source architecture earns no Result credit. A run that does not launch, exceeds a resource limit, or produces no parseable translated PDF scores zero. A valid but incomplete translation is still scored, under ceilings: omitting or leaving untranslated at least 25 % of the substantive units caps the total at 35, a material reversal of meaning caps it at 45, and repeated corruption of formulas or values caps it at 40. The lowest applicable ceiling bounds the sum of the dimension scores. A valid PDF without alignment and viewer artifacts is capped at 75, which separates missing functionality from execution failure.
paragraphs.zh: 六个结果维度中，语义完整性和术语分配了 35 分，科学对象和数据的保真度分配了 35 分，页面和阅读结构分配了 12 分，对齐可审计性分配了 8 分，离线查看器分配了 8 分，交付完整性和可访问性分配了 2 分，因此有 70 分与翻译内容相关。 评估者会检查最终整合包、渲染后的页面及其几何结构，以及浏览器中的查看器；源架构不会获得任何结果分数。 如果运行程序未能启动、超出资源限制或未能生成可解析的翻译 PDF，则得分为零。 有效但未完成的翻译仍会被评分，但受上限限制：若遗漏或未翻译至少 25% 的实质性单元，总分上限为 35 分；若出现重大语义倒置，上限为 45 分；若公式或数值反复损坏，上限为 40 分。 适用的最低上限将决定各维度分数的总和。 一个有效但缺少对齐和查看器相关功能的 PDF，其得分上限为 75 分，这区分了功能缺失与执行失败的情况。

paragraphs.en: Builder development and candidate evaluation run as separate Harbor tasks. The builder’s writable workspace holds the delivery and its permitted dependencies. The public package exposes the requirement and the development cases; the hidden cases and the evaluator stay outside it. Candidate snapshots execute in an environment built for the task, with pinned fixtures, services, and resource limits, and route model requests through the evaluator. Optimization also keeps the source benchmark’s native executor and grader. OpenHands runs record both the product’s own observations and a separate outcome ledger, so an audit can compare what the agent reports with the state it changed.
paragraphs.zh: 构建器开发和候选评估作为独立的 Harbor 任务运行。 构建器的可写工作区包含交付物及其允许的依赖项。 公共包暴露了需求和发展用例；隐藏的用例和评估器则位于其外部。 候选快照在为该任务构建的环境中执行，其中固定了设施、服务和资源限制，并通过评估器路由模型请求。 优化过程还保留了源基准的原生执行器和评分器。 OpenHands 运行记录既包括产品自身的观察结果，也包括一个独立的成果日志，以便审计时可以比较智能体报告的内容与其实际改变的状态。

paragraphs.en: Optimization evaluates the starter afresh in every builder run, which measures how much a native objective varies when the same agent is evaluated again. Across the independent measurements of each benchmark (four on BrowseComp, five elsewhere), the starter score has a standard deviation of 10.4 on BrowseComp, 4.5 on τ 3 \tau^{3} , 14.5 on TerminalBench, 20.8 on PinchBench, and 7.8 on OSWorld.
paragraphs.zh: 优化过程在每次构建运行中都会重新评估初始智能体，以此衡量当同一智能体再次被评估时，其原生目标函数发生了多大程度的变化。 在各个基准测试的独立测量中（BrowseComp 有 4 次，其他测试各有 5 次），初始得分的标准差在 BrowseComp 上为 10.4，在 τ 3 \tau^{3} 上为 4.5，在 TerminalBench 上为 14.5，在 PinchBench 上为 20.8，在 OSWorld 上为 7.8。

paragraphs.en: The static assessment of Section 5.3 applies only to Creation, where the builder writes the entire agent. It grades each frozen Creation source once, without executing it, as in model-based code evaluation ( Zhuo, 2024 ; Tong & Zhang, 2024 ; Seo et al., 2025 ) , with the judge configuration used for Result ( Table 9 ). Its shared rubric assigns 20 points to how well the mechanisms cover the requirements; 15 each to interface and lifecycle, to analysis and evidence integrity, and to safety, privacy, and side effects; 10 each to recovery and honest failure, to testability and observability, and to maintainability and generalization; and 5 to resource discipline. Figure 9 shows the total next to held-out Result. The mean static score across the 50 runs is 41.8.
paragraphs.zh: 第 5.3 节的静态评估仅适用于“创建”环节，即构建者编写整个智能体的情况。 该评估对每个已固化的“创建”源仅评分一次，且无需执行，类似于基于模型代码的评估方法（Zhuo, 2024；Tong & Zhang, 2024；Seo et al., 2025），其中使用的评审配置与“结果”部分相同（表 9）。 其通用评分标准将 20 分分配给机制对需求的覆盖程度；各分配 15 分给接口与生命周期、分析与证据完整性，以及安全性、隐私性和副作用；各分配 10 分给恢复与诚实失败、可测试性与可观察性，以及可维护性与泛化能力；并分配 5 分给资源纪律。 图 9 显示了与预留“结果”相邻的总分。 在 50 次运行中，静态评分的平均值为 41.8。

sents.en: The behavioral analysis finds candidates specialized to the visible task categories in 14 runs; the four runs in which this is the primary cause account for 56 of the 125 held-out instances on which a candidate scores below its starter.
sents.zh: 行为分析发现，在 14 次运行中，候选智能体专门针对可见的任务类别进行了优化；其中，有 4 次运行是造成这种情况的主要原因，这些运行涉及 125 个保留集实例中的 56 个，在这些实例上，候选智能体的得分低于其初始得分。

paragraphs.en: In nine runs no later round beats the first, and in 19 the selected round leads the runner-up by at most one solved development case, including eight ties broken toward the earliest round. Selection on development splits of 10 to 50 cases therefore contributes to the development gain of the selected candidate, alongside the case-specific candidates above; the held-out split measures the gain that the delivery carries.
paragraphs.zh: 在九次运行中，没有后续轮次能超越第一轮；而在十九次运行中，所选轮次与亚军之间最多仅相差一个已解决的开发案例，其中八次平局最终判定为最早出现的轮次获胜。 因此，在包含 10 至 50 个案例的开发子集中进行选择，会促进所选候选人的开发增益，同时也会受到上述特定案例候选人的影响；而预留子集则用于衡量交付所带来的增益。

paragraphs.en: The audit reads three kinds of evidence: the builder trajectory with the feedback it received, the frozen source or candidate diff, and the delivered agent’s held-out execution trace. A run is one builder on one task, as in Section 5.1 ; a case is one held-out input. A mode is present in a run if it appears in at least one case or in the builder trajectory, and modes can co-occur. Labels proposed with AI assistance were reviewed by the authors against these records. Where a report names a primary cause, it is the failure that cost the run the most points.
paragraphs.zh: 审计包含三种证据：构建器轨迹及其收到的反馈、冻结的源代码或候选差异，以及已交付智能体的保留执行轨迹。 一次运行指一个构建器处理一项任务（如第 5.1 节所述）；一个案例指一条保留的输入数据。 如果某种模式至少出现在一个案例或构建器轨迹中，则它存在于该次运行中，且多种模式可以同时出现。 在人工智能辅助下提出的标签由作者对照这些记录进行了审核。 如果报告指出了主要原因，那么该失败就是导致此次运行损失分数最多的因素。

paragraphs.en: Nearly half of the gate failures crash within one second, most of them from Qwen3.6 and the rest from the two GPT builders; neither DeepSeek builder crashes this way. Typical causes are input parsing and attempts to install dependencies into the submission directory, which the requirements forbid and the evaluator mounts read only. The other gate failures come after substantial execution, most often when the agent’s own check rejects its output and the agent reports the failure.
paragraphs.zh: 近一半的关卡失败发生在第一秒内，其中大部分来自 Qwen3.6，其余则来自两个 GPT 构建器；DeepSeek 构建器没有以这种方式崩溃。 典型原因包括输入解析以及尝试将依赖项安装到提交目录中，而需求文件禁止此类操作，且评估器将该目录以只读方式挂载。 其他关卡失败发生在执行进行较长时间之后，通常是在智能体自身的检查拒绝其输出，并报告失败时发生。

paragraphs.en: For Creation and Optimization the unit is the builder’s final report, including any completion summary written into the frozen artifact. We compare it with the actions the trajectory records, the files and capabilities the delivery contains, and the development feedback the builder received, and count a report as unsupported only when those records contradict it. A held-out failure by itself does not count against a report about development testing.
paragraphs.zh: 对于创建与优化而言，其单位是构建者的最终报告，包括写入已固化成果中的任何完成摘要。 我们将其与轨迹记录中的操作、交付内容中包含的文件和能力，以及构建者收到的开发反馈进行比较，并且只有当这些记录与报告相矛盾时，才会认为该报告缺乏支持。 单独一次被保留的失败并不会对有关开发测试的报告产生负面影响。

paragraphs.en: All nine unsupported reports assert completion. None of the 21 reports that admit partial completion or failure is contradicted by the record. Four of the six unsupported Creation reports assert that code works or was verified, while the trajectory shows that the code, or the path the report vouches for, never ran in its final form. GPT-5.6 Sol, for example, reports that its final repository-repair entrypoint emits the required reports for both development cases, yet the frozen file differs from every version the builder ran. The other two contradict feedback or audits the builder had already seen: Qwen3.6 calls its web-research agent complete and validated, with all citations resolving, one round after the judge scored both development cases 5 and reported no matching citations. In Optimization, DeepSeek-V4-Flash reports that two PinchBench tasks stayed at zero in every round, while its own development record shows one of them at 36 and 22, and it omits the four regressions it had recorded for the delivered round.
paragraphs.zh: 所有九份缺乏依据的报告都声称任务已完成。 在承认部分完成或失败的21份报告中，没有任何一份与记录相矛盾。 六份缺乏依据的“创建”报告中有四份声称代码有效或已验证，但运行轨迹显示，这些代码或报告所证实的路径从未以最终形式运行过。 例如，GPT-5.6 Sol报告称，其最终的仓库修复入口点生成了两个开发案例所需的报告，但被冻结的文件与构建者运行过的任何版本都不同。 另外两份报告则与构建者此前已看到的反馈或审计结果相矛盾：Qwen3.6称其网络研究智能体已完成并通过验证，所有引用均有效，然而在一轮评估中，评审员对两个开发案例的评分均为5，且报告称没有匹配的引用。 在“优化”部分，DeepSeek-V4-Flash报告称有两个PinchBench任务在所有轮次中得分均为零，但其自身的开发记录显示其中一个任务的得分分别为36和22，并且它遗漏了已交付版本中记录的四项性能倒退情况。

paragraphs.en: In Editing the speaker is the delivered agent, and its runtime claim is checked against effect logs, state, and output artifacts on each held-out case; a run counts if any case contains a contradiction, and 13 of the 33 runs that deliver do. On OpenHands test 006, for example, the agent describes a workspace commit as applied exactly once, while the world records zero local applies and the local manifest still lacks the file that exists only remotely.
